subject.title: refactor(delivery): centralize durable queue routing metadata

question: Should the protected maintainer-owned delivery-state refactor be sponsored for merge after a current-main rebase and final persistent-queue review?
rationale: The patch appears focused and has credible runtime proof, but it changes durable recovery metadata and carries the protected `maintainer` label, which requires explicit human handling rather than automated disposition.

options.title: Rebase and sponsor merge
options.body: Refresh the branch against current main, confirm the durable queue tests and Gateway recovery proof still cover the merge result, then merge the single-owner refactor.

options.title: Pause for broader queue review
options.body: Keep the PR open if maintainers want to compare the refactor against newer main-branch delivery ownership changes before choosing the permanent metadata boundary.

recommendation.title: Rebase and sponsor merge
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch against current main, confirm the durable queue tests and Gateway recovery proof still cover the merge result, then merge the single-owner refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this contributor directly to the proposed delivery-queue ownership refactor; broader ownership provenance could not be collected because the read-only repository command backend failed.
